worked: Married filing combined (joint federal), ages 68 and 60. Each person's own age counts: person 0 is 68, person 1 is 60, so one 1,600 amount. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 80,000.00 = 80,000.00. Federal taxable income = 80,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (including the additional amount for age 65) = 46,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 80,000.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 80,000.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 80,000.00 - 0.00 = 80,000.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 0.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for age 65 or older = 33,100.00. Line 26 subtotal 80,000.00 - 0.00 - 33,100.00 = 46,900.00. Line 29 taxable income 46,900.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 1,313.00 = 32.825 + 3% x 1,313.00 = 39.39 + 3.5% x 1,313.00 = 45.955 + 4% x 1,313.00 = 52.52 + 4.5% x 1,313.00 = 59.085 + 4.7% x 37,709.00 = 1772.323; total 2028.358 = 2,028.36. The chart and Tax Calculation Worksheet (instructions p21) round to the dollar and give 2028; expected keeps the bands. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 80,000.00 - Line 8 0.00 = 80,000.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 80,000.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
